defects.claim_says: operative on 2026-10-14, 'carried as continuing on a disclosed limited basis' because no held source shows when the review was completed
defects.source_says: The held text reads 'Immediately upon the effective date of this Order, FEMA shall review, and initiate necessary revisions of, all FEMA regulations...'. This is a one-time transitional command tied to 1988-11-18. The claim itself calls it transitional; absence of a performance date is not a legal basis for a continuing predicate (owner ruling 2026-10-28: disclosure is not evidence; if whether it happened is unknown the question stays open). The clause needs either an evidenced exhaustion or an open first-end gap, and unresolved_material_gaps is empty.

defects.claim_says: operative on 2026-10-14 on a disclosed limited basis
defects.source_says: Same defect: 'Immediately upon the effective date of this Order, FEMA shall review, and initiate necessary renegotiations of, all interagency agreements...' is a one-time 1988 command; no held source supplies a continuing legal basis.

defects.claim_says: operative; the 90- and 180-day periods are deadlines for first issuance and no end is claimed
defects.source_says: Section 6(a) commands one-time issuance of interim and final directives within 90 and 180 days of 1988-11-18; the claim's own evidence (44 CFR part 352 establishing the procedures under EO 12657) indicates the directives were issued, i.e. the command was performed. Calling a performed one-time issuance command operative, with no dated or interval end and no gap recorded, is internally inconsistent.

The claim fails on clause states: sections 6(a), 6(b) and 6(c) are one-time 1988 implementation commands that the claim itself labels transitional, yet it records them as operative on 2026-10-14 with a predicate that rests only on the absence of a performance date, and lists no material gap.
